blocks.prompt: 11 An RC circuit has an emf of 12 volts, resistance \(R = 6\,\Omega\) and capacitance \(C = 3\) farad. Initially, the capacitor is uncharged. Find the current \(I(t)\) at any time \(t\).
blocks.explanation:
RC circuit: \(RC\frac{dq}{dt} = CV_S - q\) for the charge \(q\) (Example 4 (i), Section 4.1.1). Solve for \(q\) with \(q(0) = 0\), then \(I = \frac{dq}{dt}\).
The question asks for the current, not the charge.
steps:
Given: \(V_S = 12\) V, \(R = 6\ \Omega\), \(C = 3\) F, \(q(0) = 0\) (uncharged).
To find: \(I(t)\).
Method: RC model for \(q\) (separable), then differentiate: \(I = \frac{dq}{dt}\).

Write the differential equation
\[RC = 6 \times 3 = 18\]
\[CV_S = 3 \times 12 = 36\]
\[18\dfrac{dq}{dt} = 36 - q\]
Why: substitute the values into the RC model.

Separate and integrate
\[\int\dfrac{dq}{36 - q} = \int\dfrac{dt}{18}\]
\[-\ln|36 - q| = \dfrac{t}{18} + C_1\]
Why: the derivative of \(36 - q\) is \(-1\).

Use \(q(0) = 0\)
\[-\ln 36 = C_1\]
\[\ln\left|\dfrac{36 - q}{36}\right| = -\dfrac{t}{18}\]
\[q(t) = 36\left(1 - e^{-t/18}\right)\]
Why: substitute \(C_1\), combine the logarithms, take \(e\). At \(t = 0\), \(36 - q = 36 > 0\), so the \(+\) sign is taken.

Find the current
\[I = \dfrac{dq}{dt} = 36 \cdot \dfrac{1}{18}e^{-t/18}\]
\[I(t) = 2e^{-t/18}\]
Why: current is the rate of flow of charge; \(\frac{d}{dt}e^{-t/18} = -\frac{1}{18}e^{-t/18}\).

Check
\(I(0) = 2 = \frac{12}{6} = \frac{V_S}{R}\): at the start the empty capacitor takes no voltage \(\checkmark\).
\[RI + \dfrac{q}{C} = 12e^{-t/18} + 12 - 12e^{-t/18} = 12 \;\checkmark\]
